simple.meaning: נָהָה (nâhâh) is a Hebrew action word meaning “to groan , i.e. bewail ; hence (through the idea of crying aloud), to assemble (as if on proclamation).” BibleIQ anchors the English reading to this source verb before comparing its uses.
simple.biblicalBackground: This action appears 3 times in 1 Samuel, Ezekiel, Micah, beginning at 1 Samuel 7:2. The surrounding contexts include family line, Egypt, Israel.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to נָהָה (H5091) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: Actions in Scripture show what people do, what God does, and how covenant faithfulness or rebellion is described. BibleIQ compares the action across its occurrences.
simple.summary: נָהָה (nâhâh) / H5091 is traced through 1 Samuel 7:2, Ezekiel 32:18, Micah 2:4 with source-language evidence and verse context.
